subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: To find a missing angle when you know the opposite and adjacent sides, which is used?
questions.explain: With opposite and adjacent you use tan, then inverse tan to get the angle.

questions.q: What is the value of sin 90°?
questions.explain: sin 90° = 1 is a standard exact value.

questions.q: An isosceles triangle has an apex angle of 40°. What is each base angle?
questions.explain: The two equal base angles share 180° − 40° = 140°, so each is 70°.

questions.q: Three angles meet at a point and are 120°, 150° and x. What is x?
questions.explain: Angles around a point sum to 360°, so x = 360° − 120° − 150° = 90°.

questions.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a pentagon?
What is the exact value of sin 30°?
questions.explain: sin 30° = 1/2 is a standard exact value.

questions.q: What is the exact value of cos 60°?
questions.explain: cos 60° = 1/2 is a standard exact value.

questions.q: A cube has side 4 cm. What is its total surface area?
A triangle has base 10 cm and height 6 cm. What is its area?
Two angles are vertically opposite. One is 47°. What is the other?
questions.explain: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so it is 47°.

questions.q: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One angle is 75°. What is its alternate angle?
questions.explain: Alternate (Z) angles between parallel lines are equal, so it is 75°.

questions.q: An exterior angle of a regular polygon is 40°. How many sides does it have?
